DatasetRegistration.title: DatasetRegistration

deleted.description: A missing or protected resource is a Problem, never a false success receipt.

ErrorCode.description: Every Appendix D code. There is no arbitrary-string/fallback variant.

EvaluationReceipt.description: Durable, request-bound result from one engine evaluation.

EventPage.description:
Durable events only. Cross-item ordering/cursor relations are checked by
Deserialize; JSON Schema cannot express those relational constraints.
EventPage.title: EventPage

attempt_receipt.description: Actual per-attempt details when the evaluator retained them.

ExportRequest.description: Client output paths are deliberately absent: the engine writes only its store.
ExportRequest.title: ExportRequest

FeedbackRecord.description: Opt-in internal evaluation data (§13.4), not a public event or raw data row.

oneOf.description: The plan handler refuses this with CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE in v1.

MetricSample.description:
Null is unavailable, never zero. Scope and availability are extensible strings
(`device:<uuid>` and `unavailable:<reason>` respectively).

anyOf.description: Exact byte counts follow §4.1 even above JavaScript's integer range.

MetricValue.description: §9.1 includes both numeric measurements and the rust_timed_alone boolean.

ObjectiveSpec.description:
The objective grammar is owned by jope-runtime; the API transports it without
importing the evaluator. A string is a built-in name or name:param=value.

ObjectiveValidation.description:
Objective grammar resolution belongs to the runtime. Errors are structured
diagnostics; malformed request JSON is INVALID_INPUT at the HTTP boundary.
ObjectiveValidation.title: ObjectiveValidation

PredictRequest.description: Registered input avoids exposing a client-side output path to the engine.
PredictRequest.title: PredictRequest

Problem.description:
JopeDime's [RFC 9457](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9457.html) profile.

Serialize with **`Content-Type: application/problem+json`**, not the success
response media type. Set the actual HTTP response status to [`Self::status`].
The spec requires `type`, `title`, `status`, `detail` and the three required
extensions; `instance` and `field` are optional and omitted when absent.
Unknown extension members are ignored when reading the document.

`retriable` describes this occurrence. For IO_FAILURE the producer decides it
from the actual failure; for conditional policies it must also provide the
required action through `remedy`. Catalog `maybe` is not silently made false.
Problem.title: Problem

PublicEvent.description:
Only durable events have this envelope. Telemetry is a separate SSE payload.
Publication/sequence allocation belongs to SVC-04, after transaction commit.

time.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp; produced by the service clock.

evaluation_receipt.description: Full Q1 request receipt, atomically committed with this terminal event.

overrides.description: With warm_start, the service must also verify unchanged ProblemDigest.

RunOverrides.description:
Only fields supplied here change the parent RunSpec. Seed selection, dry-run
and plan binding are separate mechanisms, so they cannot be overridden here.

test_dataset.description: Missing inherits; explicit null removes the parent's external test dataset.

next_after.description: Opaque continuation token; null denotes the end of the list.

RunSnapshot.description: The watermark, rather than revision, is the long-poll/attach cursor (§4.4).

evaluation_receipt.description: Present only for engine evaluations using the versioned Q1 receipt path.

RunSnapshot.title: RunSnapshot

RunSpec.description: Operation 6 uses this same body for a dry-run plan and a real start.

device.description: `auto`, `cpu`, or an explicit device such as `cuda:0`.

RunSpec.title: RunSpec

TelemetryEvent.description: Ephemeral SSE frame: deliberately lacks `sequence` and therefore no SSE id.
TelemetryEvent.title: TelemetryEvent
